title: Catering Sales Standards for Meetings & Events: Proposal, Option Period and Signature
content:
A Meetings & Events contract begins as a proposal from catering sales, which holds the function space on a tentative basis, and becomes definite when the client signs it.

## Standards

1. **What may be proposed.** Catering sales proposes a package only for an expected attendance between the package's fewest and most attendees sold, and only for an event no more than the package's booking-window figure of calendar days away.
2. **Who signs.** The client signs the contract themselves. Signing commits the client to the food and beverage minimum, the guarantee rules and the cancellation scale, so guest services never signs on the client's behalf.
3. **Option period.** The contract can be signed only within the package's option period of calendar days after the proposal was issued. Days are counted as whole calendar days from the proposal date, which is day zero; a signature on the last day of the option period is accepted.
4. **Lapse.** A tentative contract whose option period ends unsigned lapses, and its function space is released.
5. **Menus.** Menus are confirmed no later than the package's menu-deadline figure of calendar days before the event.

## The option period, condition by condition

| Element | What governs it |
|---|---|
| The record the clock starts from | The proposal date recorded on the event contract |
| Day zero | The proposal date itself |
| Unit | Whole calendar days |
| Length | The package's option period |
| Last day on which a signature is accepted | The day whose count equals the option period |
| Signature after that day | Not possible; the tentative contract lapses and the space is released |

## Hypothetical boundary cases

Hypothetical inputs: a package with an option period of 10 calendar days and a proposal issued on 3 March.
- 3 March is day zero and 13 March is day 10.
- A client signature on 13 March falls on the last day of the option period and is accepted; the contract becomes definite.
- On 14 March the option period has ended; a contract still unsigned has lapsed and the space has been released, so it can no longer be signed.
- A signature on 6 March, day 3, is within the option period.

## Points of judgement

- **Whose signature counts?** Only the client's own; guest services never signs on the client's behalf.
- **What happens at the end of an unsigned option period?** When the option period passes without a signed contract, the tentative contract is cancelled and its function space is released.
